ck_cm_def.source: H. Cohn, A. Kumar, Universally optimal distribution of points on spheres, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 20 (2007), 99-148
ck_cm_def.text: Recall that a C^infinity function f : I -> R on an interval I is completely monotonic if (-1)^k f^(k)(x) >= 0 for all x in I and all k >= 0 (see [Wid, p. 145]) ... It might seem preferable to use completely monotonic functions of distance, rather than squared distance, but squared distance is in fact more natural than it first appears ... it is more general than using distance: it is not hard to prove that if r -> f(r^2) is completely monotonic on a subinterval (a,b) of (0,infinity), then f is completely monotonic on (a^2,b^2), but not vice versa.
